title: Monoidal pullback counit equals the canonical structure-sheaf comparison
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be an arbitrary morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $j^*$ be Mathlib\'s pullback functor on sheaves of modules [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], equipped with the monoidal structure descended from presheaf pullback and sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Its monoidal counit $\eta:j^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Z$ equals the canonical structure-sheaf pullback map, namely the adjoint of the structure-ring map $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_Z$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. In Lean this is $\operatorname{Functor.OplaxMonoidal.\eta}(\operatorname{pullback}j)=(\operatorname{pullbackObjUnitIso}j).\operatorname{hom}$. No immersion, invertibility, tensor-exponent, or square-zero hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01CD, the unit part of canonical tensor pullback.

proof.text: Apply the pullback-pushforward adjunction hom-equivalence. Mathlib's pullbackPushforwardAdjunction_homEquiv_pullbackObjUnitToUnit identifies the image of the canonical structure-sheaf map with unitToPushforwardObjUnit, the ring map.

Expand the descended monoidal counit and precompose by pullback of the sheafification unit, which is an isomorphism. Apply the composite adjunction hom-equivalence. The sheafification/pullback comparison is leftAdjointUniq for the two composite adjunctions; homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app removes this comparison. Cancel the sheafification counit by homEquiv_counit, and use adjunctionOfCommRingCat_homEquiv_η to identify the remaining presheaf counit with the lax pushforward unit. On the other side use pullbackPushforwardAdjunction_homEquiv_pullbackObjUnitToUnit and cancel the sheafification counit. The resulting presheaf maps are equal sectionwise: restrictScalars_η identifies their values with the structure-ring homomorphism. No unproved intermediate statement is used.
Injectivity of the adjunction hom-equivalence identifies the two sheaf morphisms. The argument is functorial for arbitrary j; in particular it also covers empty schemes and identity morphisms.
